target_customer: Minecraft players, plus server owners and game creators who earn revenue from hosted games
problem: Joining modded Minecraft games needs mod installation and setup, and creators lack a simple way to host and earn from games.
business_model: Platform with creator revenue share and hosting, pitched as Roblox style on top of Minecraft
product_category: Game launcher and creator platform for Minecraft

founders.name: Ali Kavoosi
education: University of Oxford, PhD student in Healthcare AI (per Simplifine launch post on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on optimizing AI models, from Deep Brain Stimulators to GPU training and inference speed.

technical_complexity.rationale: One click join with automatic mod delivery and hosting needs a launcher, mod distribution and server orchestration, standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Value would grow with creators and players on the platform, but no evidence of that scale was found and Minecraft launchers are many.

market_need_then: The YC page cites 312M Minecraft players as the base. Independent evidence of demand for a mini game launcher was not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Several unrelated products and YC listings use the Orca name, and no brand coverage was found.

pivots.to: Browser based product to play, mod and host Minecraft with AI
pivots.why: A Product Hunt launch dated Feb 2026 is reported by a search summary for a product named Orca. The link to this exact company is not certain.

outcome_analysis: Orca Client is listed as active with a team of two. No funding, user numbers or press were found, so its traction is unknown. It appears to have continued product work into 2026, possibly moving to a browser based AI modding product, but that identification is uncertain.
notes: The company website returned HTTP 402 so it could not be read. Funding: CB Insights profiles of unclear identity show 120K seed (2023) and 500K pre-seed (May 2024); not attributed to this company. A third party profile names Ege Kaan Duman as co-founder and CEO and a former founder Raveen Kariyawasam, but the YC page lists only Ali Kavoosi, so only he is recorded. Competitor searches returned undated alternative lists, so the dated list is empty. Several other YC companies share the Orca name.
